Q: Exclusive load and store instructions require enabled caches on real hardware (Cortex-A53) A:

The A53's exclusive monitor lives in the data cache unit. It only tracks the reservation if the lock's RAM is mapped as cacheable Normal memory with the data cache enabled. I'd map the mutex region that way and keep the D-cache on.

With non-cacheable memory or the D-cache off, LDXR goes out on the bus with Excl set. The A53 then relies on an external global monitor in the interconnect or memory controller. But if that monitor isn't present, which is the case on the Pi 3B+, STXR will just keep failing and the spin loop never exits. QEMU doesn't reproduce this failure, so it works there.

Q: Is it possible to make a Test Method generic while using MSTest as test framework? A:

I haven't tested this myself yet, but in march of 2025, MSTest 3.8 released and they reportedly added support for generic test methods: https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/mstest-3-8-highlights/

Better data-driven tests: Parameterized generic test methods are now supported.

This is also mentioned on their learn page for data driven testing: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/testing/unit-testing-mstest-writing-tests-data-driven#generic-test-methods

Starting with MSTest v3.8, a TestMethod can have type parameters. The framework infers type arguments from DataRow or DynamicData values:

[TestMethod]
[DataRow(42)]
[DataRow("alpha")]
public void Value_RoundTrips<T>(T value)
{
    Assert.AreEqual(value, value);
}

Q: How to make this stream gatherer threadsafe? A:

Is my understanding correct or is the stream framework internally synchronizes access to the state objects while performing combiner and finisher operations?

This is closest to the truth. Explicit synchronization isn't exactly how it works, but those processing objects are not expected to be thread-safe.
